MPO Policy Committee and CMAP Board

Federal legislation expands FAU funding to include public transit infrastructure improvements, in addition
to roads� The CATS Policy Committee is designated as the metropolitan planning organization (MPO)
pursuant to the 1973 Federal Highway Act�

The Executive Committee programs transportation projects, balancing funding allotments among
the regional councils and approving council-to-council fund borrowing. The Executive Committee also
establishes policies related to the FAU program�

A public transit financial crisis hits; the Regional Transportation Authority is reorganized and PACE
Suburban Bus is created�

The federal Intermodal Surface Transportation Efficiency Act (ISTEA) creates the Surface Transportation
Program (STP), a new block grant program that replaces the FAU program; authorizes funding for the
Congestion Mitigation and Air Quality Improvement Program (CMAQ), which is administered by IDOT;
and requires Illinois to set aside 10% of STP funds for project beyond roads and transit� The state creates
the Illinois Transportation Enhancement Program�
In response to the ISTEA, the Executive Committee refines council boundaries and ensures that every
municipality is eligible for funding (a departure from the past when only those within the urbanized
boundary were eligible)� The Executive Committee is involved in the implementation of ISTEA beyond
the programming of funds: hey sponsor studies exploring the potential for increased transit service in the
region; produce and distribute a video describing and addressing the ozone problem; and develop bicycle
and pedestrian plans for each of the councils�

The Regional Planning Act establishes the Chicago Metropolitan Agency for Planning (CMAP) for
integrated land use (formerly NIPC) and transportation (formerly CATS) planning�

The GO TO 2040 comprehensive regional plan is adopted by the CMAP Board and MPO Policy
Committee�

The USDOT’s federal certification review encourages CMAP to move away from the sub-allocation of
STP funds and instead expand performance-based programming of STP funds.

The FHWA and the FTA finalize new planning regulations in response to changes included in the MAP-21
Act and the FAST Act� The regulations continue an insistence that STP formula allocations are inconsistent
with current law�

CMAP convenes a working group of COM Executive Committee members, CDOT, IDOT, and the FHWA to
discuss reforms to the STP suballocation and project selection process�

The ON TO 2050 comprehensive regional plan is adopted by the CMAP Board and MPO Policy
Committee�

The ON TO 2050 comprehensive plan is updated and adopted by the CMAP Board and MPO Policy
Committee�
